collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: An elder relative gently encourages a young villager to move into a hut of their own: say not yet, or try it for a week.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is old enough to move into (subject.his/her) own hut, and (friend), (friend.his/her) elder relative, has been gently encouraging (subject.him/her) to. "It would be good for you," (friend) says. "Your own space. Your own way of doing things." (subject) likes (subject.his/her) family's hut. (subject.He/she) isn't sure (subject.he/she) is ready.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Not yet," says (subject). "Maybe next season." (friend) looks like (friend.he/she) wants to argue, then doesn't. "Alright. It's your choice." (subject) stays. The next season comes, and (subject.he/she) still isn't ready. Then one day, without anyone saying anything, (subject.he/she) is. (subject.He/she) starts building. (friend) helps, and says nothing about being right, because (friend.he/she) wasn't, exactly. It just happened later.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "What if I try it for a week?" says (subject). (subject.He/she) borrows an empty hut. The first night is strange and too quiet. The second is less strange. By the end of the week (subject.he/she) has rearranged everything three times. (subject.He/she) goes back home anyway. "I liked it," (subject.he/she) tells (friend). "I'm just not done here yet." (friend) nods. That's an answer too.
